paragraphes: At school, things keep disappearing from the lockers. The cleaners see it first.
They tell the principal. Months later, the school buys locks. The money is small and it comes late.
In a company, a good idea can start at the bottom and go up. This is called bottom-up. It can also start at the top and go down. This is called top-down.

decouverte.titre: It is like the school rules
decouverte.comme: In one school, the principal writes the rules and tells every student. In another school, students report a problem and the principal reacts.
decouverte.enVrai: Top-down: senior leaders learn about the laws and the dangers. Then they send plans and rules down to everyone. Bottom-up: the IT department sees a problem. The IT department is the team that looks after the computers. It tells the leaders and asks for help and money. A real company can mix both ways.

decouverte.question: The IT team sees a danger, but the leaders do not know about it. What happens most often?
options: The company is ready before any attack
The money arrives late, after the problems
Everyone follows the rules from day one
decouverte.answer: The money arrives late, after the problems
decouverte.explanation: Without a decision from the top, people react after the problem. Money is short. The other two answers fit top-down better.

decouverte.texte: The director of a bank reads the laws that protect customers. She asks for a security plan for the whole bank, with a budget. The teams follow it. This is top-down. One day, a technician sees tricky emails. She writes to the boss to ask for tools. This is bottom-up.

decouverte.comme: You wear a helmet before you ride a bike. That is preventing. You buy a helmet after a fall. That is reacting.
decouverte.enVrai: A proactive measure gets ready before a problem. A reactive measure answers after it. Top-down is mostly proactive. Bottom-up is mostly reactive, and it often comes too late.

cards.question: Official definition: “top-down approach”
cards.answer: In a top-down approach, senior leadership starts by understanding the regulations and security threats faced by the organization, and initiates strategies, policies, and guidelines that are pushed down throughout the rest of the organization.
cards.explanation: The leaders learn about the laws and the dangers first. Then they send plans and rules down to everyone.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “top-down approach”?
options: In a top-down approach, the IT department starts by understanding the regulations and security threats faced by the organization, and initiates strategies, policies, and guidelines that are pushed up to senior leadership.

In a top-down approach, senior leadership starts by understanding the regulations and security threats faced by the organization, and waits for problems before it initiates strategies, policies, and guidelines.

In a top-down approach, senior leadership starts by understanding the regulations and security threats faced by the organization, and initiates strategies, policies, and guidelines that are pushed down throughout the rest of the organization.

In a top-down approach, senior leadership starts by understanding the budget and business goals of the organization, and initiates strategies, policies, and guidelines that are pushed down throughout the rest of the organization.
options_why: This mixes the roles. In top-down, senior leadership starts, and the plans go down, not up.
Top-down is proactive. The leaders do not wait for problems to happen.
The real sentence starts from the regulations and the security threats, not from the budget.
cards.answer: In a top-down approach, senior leadership starts by understanding the regulations and security threats faced by the organization, and initiates strategies, policies, and guidelines that are pushed down throughout the rest of the organization.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: senior leadership starts, regulations and security threats, pushed down.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “top-down approach” from memory.
cards.answer: In a top-down approach, senior leadership starts by understanding the regulations and security threats faced by the organization, and initiates strategies, policies, and guidelines that are pushed down throughout the rest of the organization.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the leaders start, they learn laws and threats, and they push plans down.

cards.question: Official definition: “bottom-up approach”
cards.answer: Historically, enterprises have utilized more of a bottom-up approach to security, in which the IT department takes security seriously and attempts to develop a security function for the company.
cards.explanation: In the past, the IT team often started security by itself. It cared about security and tried to build it for the company.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “bottom-up approach”?
options: Historically, enterprises have utilized more of a bottom-up approach to security, in which the IT department takes security seriously and attempts to develop a security function for the company.
Historically, enterprises have utilized more of a bottom-up approach to security, in which senior leadership takes security seriously and attempts to develop a security function for the company.
Historically, enterprises have utilized more of a bottom-up approach to security, in which the IT department takes security seriously and receives a full budget from the company.
Historically, enterprises have utilized more of a top-down approach to security, in which the IT department takes security seriously and attempts to develop a security function for the company.
options_why: In bottom-up, the IT department starts, not senior leadership.
The IT department attempts to develop a security function. A full budget is often the problem, not the starting point.
The real sentence says bottom-up. A top-down approach starts with the leaders.
cards.answer: Historically, enterprises have utilized more of a bottom-up approach to security, in which the IT department takes security seriously and attempts to develop a security function for the company.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: bottom-up, the IT department, attempts to develop a security function.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “bottom-up approach” from memory.
cards.answer: Historically, enterprises have utilized more of a bottom-up approach to security, in which the IT department takes security seriously and attempts to develop a security function for the company.
cards.explanation: Three parts: an old habit (historically), the IT department acts, and it tries to build a security function.

cards.question: The leaders of a company read the laws. Then they send a security plan to every team. Which approach is this?
options: Bottom-up, because every team must act
Top-down
Reactive, because the plan follows the laws
Neither, because only the IT team can start security
options_why: Bottom-up means the idea starts with the teams. Here the leaders start.
Reading the laws in advance is proactive. The leaders act before a problem.
Leaders can start security too. That is exactly what top-down means.
cards.answer: Top-down
cards.explanation: The decision starts with the leaders and goes down through the company. That is top-down.

cards.question: A technician sees tricky emails going around. She tells her boss and asks for a budget. Which approach is this?
options: Top-down: the leaders already decided
Top-down: the boss now owns the idea
Neither: asking for a budget is not an approach
Bottom-up: the idea starts with the IT team
options_why: The leaders have decided nothing yet. They do not even know about the problem.
The idea started with the technician, so it started at the bottom.
The path from the field up to the leaders is exactly the bottom-up approach.
cards.answer: Bottom-up: the idea starts with the IT team
cards.explanation: The finding goes up from the field to the leaders. It goes from the bottom up.

cards.question: Which approach is usually proactive?
options: Bottom-up: the IT team plans before problems happen
Top-down: the leaders plan before problems happen
Both are always proactive, with no exception
Neither: only an attack can start a security plan
options_why: Bottom-up usually reacts after the problems. The leaders are not yet involved.
The words always and no exception are a warning sign. Bottom-up is often reactive.
A plan can start before any attack. That is what proactive means.
cards.answer: Top-down: the leaders plan before problems happen
cards.explanation: The leaders look ahead at laws and threats and start plans in advance.

cards.question: A company has no security plan. The IT team has asked for money three times, but the leaders say no. What is the BEST way to fix the root cause?
options: Buy tools with money taken from other teams
Wait for an attack to happen, so that the leaders will listen
Ask the IT team to write stricter rules and enforce them alone
Get senior leaders to own security and send a plan down
options_why: This treats the symptom. There is still no plan and no support from the top.
This is reactive and risky. A manager prevents the problem instead.
Rules without the support of the leaders are not followed or paid for.
cards.answer: Get senior leaders to own security and send a plan down
cards.explanation: The root cause is that the leaders do not own security. Top-down fixes this.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”: bottom-up often leads to underfunded programs.

cards.question: Which statement about the bottom-up approach is NOT true?
options: It often gives reactive measures
It often leads to underfunded security programs
It is the most proactive way to protect a company
The IT team pushes its findings up to senior management
options_why: This is true, so it is not the answer. Bottom-up often reacts after the problem.
This is true, so it is not the answer. The leaders have not made security a priority.
This is true, so it is not the answer. This is how the approach works.
cards.answer: It is the most proactive way to protect a company
cards.explanation: Bottom-up often gives reactive measures, not proactive ones.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: What is the MOST important benefit of top-down security?
options: The senior leaders support it, so it becomes a priority
It needs no budget at all because the IT team works for free
It makes technical tools unnecessary in the whole company
It stops every attack before it can happen
options_why: Security always costs something. Top-down just makes money easier to get.
Tools are still needed. Top-down only sets the direction for them.
No approach stops every attack. This extreme answer is a warning sign.
cards.answer: The senior leaders support it, so it becomes a priority
cards.explanation: When the most senior executives support security, it becomes a priority and matches the company strategy.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: What should a company do FIRST to build strong governance for a top-down approach?
options: Align with one or more security control frameworks
Buy a firewall for each office
Ask every worker to write a personal rule
Choose the tools that have the best prices
options_why: A tool without a plan is a technical answer to a management question.
Rules written alone do not give the company one direction.
Price is a later choice. First the leaders need a direction.
cards.answer: Align with one or more security control frameworks
cards.explanation: Strong governance starts with alignment with one or more security control frameworks.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: The leaders set the rules (top-down). The IT team also reports new dangers upward (bottom-up). What does the manual say about using both?
options: Only one approach is allowed in each company
The two approaches cannot work together
Security can be managed with a mix of the two
The bottom-up part must be removed after one year
options_why: The manual does not forbid a mix. It says the two can be combined.
They can. Leaders decide from above and the teams inform from below.
The manual gives no such rule. This detail is invented.
cards.answer: Security can be managed with a mix of the two
cards.explanation: The manual says security management can be top-down, bottom-up, or some combination of the two.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: A company writes a new rule after a data leak happened. Is this a proactive or a reactive measure?
options: Proactive: it protects the company in advance
Proactive, because every rule is written in advance
Neither, because rules are not security measures
Reactive: it answers after the problem
options_why: The leak has already happened. The rule comes after it.
A rule can also be written after a problem. The timing is what matters.
Rules are security measures. They are management controls.
cards.answer: Reactive: it answers after the problem
cards.explanation: The rule answers a problem that already happened. That is reactive.

cards.question: Which approach is LEAST likely to give security the budget it needs?
options: Top-down
Bottom-up
A mix of top-down and bottom-up
Top-down with strong governance
options_why: Here the leaders support security, so money is easier to get.
The leaders are part of the mix, so budget support is more likely.
This is the strongest case for getting the budget.
cards.answer: Bottom-up
cards.explanation: In bottom-up the IT team must first convince the leaders, which often leads to underfunded programs.

cards.question: Who starts the plan in a top-down approach?
cards.answer: The senior leaders. They send plans and rules down to everyone.
cards.explanation: Think of the principal who writes the school rules.

cards.question: Why do bottom-up programs often have too little money?
cards.answer: The leaders have not decided that security is a priority. The IT team must first convince them.
cards.explanation: Without a decision from the top, money arrives late, often after a problem.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Say in your own words the difference between proactive and reactive.
cards.answer: Proactive: you act before the problem. Reactive: you act after it.
cards.explanation: Think of the helmet before the fall and the helmet after the fall.

cards.question: Can a company use both top-down and bottom-up?
cards.answer: Yes. The leaders decide from the top and the IT team reports from the bottom. The manual says a mix is possible.
cards.explanation: A mix gives decisions from above and information from below.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

paragraphes: Your home has many protections. There is a lock, an alarm and a neighbor who watches. There is also a rule: we lock the door at night.
Some protections are objects. Some are people. Some are written rules.
In cybersecurity, each protection like this is called a security control.

decouverte.comme: The lock and the alarm are machines. The neighbor who watches is a person. The rule “lock the door” is written for everyone.
decouverte.enVrai: A technical control is a system that protects, like a firewall. A firewall filters the traffic on a network. An operational control is done by people, like a security guard. A management control is a written rule, like a policy. A policy is an official rule of the company.

decouverte.question: A guard watches the door of the building. What type of control is this?
options: Technical
Operational
Management
decouverte.explanation: A guard is a person, not a system. Technical means machine. Management means written rule.

decouverte.texte: A bank has a firewall to filter its network. It has a guard at the entrance. It also has a rule: never lend your badge. These are three controls of three types. Together they protect better than one alone.

decouverte.comme: A smoke detector spots a fire. An extinguisher fights it. A no-smoking rule stops it from starting.
decouverte.enVrai: A control can prevent a threat, detect it, minimize its damage, or counteract it. To counteract means to act against something. The same control can do more than one job.

decouverte.titre: Three technical tools from the manual
decouverte.texte: An IDS spots an intruder and warns you. An IPS spots the intruder and blocks it. A DLP tool stops secret data from leaving the company. DLP means data loss prevention. These three tools are systems, so they are technical controls.

cards.question: Official definition: “security control”
cards.answer: A security control is a technical, operational, or management safeguard used to prevent, detect, minimize, or counteract security threats.
cards.explanation: A control is any protection against threats. It can be a machine, a person or a rule. It can stop, spot, reduce or fight a threat.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “security control”?
options: A security control is a technical, operational, or management safeguard used only to detect and report security threats.
A security control is a technical, operational, or management safeguard used to prevent, detect, minimize, or counteract security threats.
A security control is a technical, physical, or management safeguard used to prevent, detect, minimize, or counteract security threats.
A security control is a technical, operational, or management safeguard used to prevent, detect, accept, or ignore security threats.
options_why: Only is the trap. A control can also prevent, minimize or counteract a threat.
In this sentence the three types are technical, operational and management. Physical is not named.
A control does not accept or ignore a threat. The verbs are prevent, detect, minimize, counteract.
cards.answer: A security control is a technical, operational, or management safeguard used to prevent, detect, minimize, or counteract security threats.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: technical, operational, or management, and prevent, detect, minimize, counteract.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “security control” from memory.
cards.answer: A security control is a technical, operational, or management safeguard used to prevent, detect, minimize, or counteract security threats.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the three types, the four verbs, and the target: threats.

cards.question: Official definition: “technical controls”
cards.answer: Technical controls are system-based safeguards and countermeasures — things like firewalls, IDS/IPS, and data loss prevention (DLP).
cards.explanation: A technical control is a system that protects. A firewall is one example.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “technical controls” from memory.
cards.answer: Technical controls are system-based safeguards and countermeasures — things like firewalls, IDS/IPS, and data loss prevention (DLP).
cards.explanation: Remember: system-based safeguards, with three examples of machines that protect.

cards.question: Official definition: “operational controls”
cards.answer: Operational controls are safeguards and countermeasures that are primarily implemented and executed by people (as opposed to systems); security guards are a common example.
cards.explanation: People do the work, not machines. A security guard is the usual example.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “operational controls” from memory.
cards.answer: Operational controls are safeguards and countermeasures that are primarily implemented and executed by people (as opposed to systems); security guards are a common example.
cards.explanation: Remember: done by people, not by systems, and the guard is the example.

cards.question: Official definition: “management controls”
cards.answer: Management controls include policies, procedures, and other countermeasures that control (or manage) the information security risk.
cards.explanation: These are written rules and steps that manage the risk.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “management controls” from memory.
cards.answer: Management controls include policies, procedures, and other countermeasures that control (or manage) the information security risk.
cards.explanation: Remember: policies, procedures, and other measures that manage the risk.

cards.question: Is a firewall a technical control or an operational control?
options: Operational: people run it all day
Management: it is a written rule
Technical: it is a system
None: a firewall is not a control
options_why: An operational control is mostly done by people. A firewall is a system.
A management control is a policy or procedure. A firewall is not written text.
A firewall is a safeguard, so it is a control.
cards.answer: Technical: it is a system
cards.explanation: A firewall is a system. Technical controls are system-based safeguards.

cards.question: A company writes a rule: “Nobody lends their badge.” What type of control is this?
options: Management: it is a written rule
Technical: it is a rule inside a system
Operational: guards check badges
None: a rule is not a control
options_why: No machine is involved. It is a written rule.
An operational control is done by people, like a guard. Here the rule is what counts.
Policies and procedures are management controls.
cards.answer: Management: it is a written rule
cards.explanation: Policies and procedures are management controls.

cards.question: Which of these is an operational control?
options: A firewall on the network
A written security policy
A data loss prevention tool
A security guard at the entrance
options_why: A firewall is a system, so it is a technical control.
A policy is a rule, so it is a management control.
A DLP tool is a system, so it is a technical control.
cards.answer: A security guard at the entrance
cards.explanation: The manual gives security guards as the common example of an operational control.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT a type of control named in the manual?
options: Technical
Financial
Operational
Management
options_why: This is one of the three types in the manual.
This is one of the three types in the manual.
This is one of the three types in the manual.
cards.answer: Financial
cards.explanation: The three types are technical, operational and management.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: A bank wants the BEST protection for its customer data. Which choice is BEST?
options: Use technical, operational and management controls together
Buy the strongest firewall available and nothing else
Write a very long policy and stop there
Hire many guards and use no systems
options_why: Tools alone leave gaps. Nobody would know what to do with them.
A rule that nobody checks or supports with tools is weak.
People alone cannot watch a network. Systems are also needed.
cards.answer: Use technical, operational and management controls together
cards.explanation: The three types complete each other. Good protection mixes machines, people and rules.

cards.question: Management controls are sometimes called “administrative controls”. What should you NOT confuse this with?
options: Rules and procedures that manage risk
A written policy of the company
The work of a security guard
The work of a system administrator (sysadmin)
options_why: This is exactly what management controls are. There is no confusion.
A policy is a management control, so it is not a confusion.
A guard is an operational control. The manual warns about sysadmins, not guards.
cards.answer: The work of a system administrator (sysadmin)
cards.explanation: Administrative here means rules and management. It is not the work of a sysadmin.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: A company uses only technical tools. It has no written rules and no trained people. Which problem is MOST likely?
options: The tools will stop working at once
The tools will block every attack by themselves
Nobody knows how to use the tools or when to act
The company will have too many written rules
options_why: The tools can still work. The problem is that nobody manages them.
No tool blocks every attack. This extreme answer is a warning sign.
The company has no written rules at all.
cards.answer: Nobody knows how to use the tools or when to act
cards.explanation: Tools need people and rules around them. The three types of controls complete each other.
cards.explanation_more: Reasoning from outside the manual, based on the three types of controls.

cards.question: Many companies stopped using the terms technical, operational and management. What reason does the manual give?
options: The lines blur: many controls fit into more than one category
A law removed the three types
They are the same as confidentiality, integrity and availability
Only technical controls are real controls
options_why: The manual does not mention a law. It speaks about confusion.
These are different ideas. They are the goals of security, not types of controls.
Operational and management controls are real controls too.
cards.answer: The lines blur: many controls fit into more than one category
cards.explanation: A rule can be applied by people and helped by a tool. So the categories can overlap.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: A hospital makes a rule that every door must be locked at night. A guard checks the doors. Which statement is BEST?
options: Both are technical controls because doors are objects
Both are management controls because the guard follows a written rule
The rule is a management control and the guard check is operational
Both are operational controls because people do both
options_why: Technical controls are systems. A rule and a guard are not systems.
The guard is a person who does the work, so that part is operational.
The rule itself is written. It is a management control.
cards.answer: The rule is a management control and the guard check is operational
cards.explanation: The rule is written (management). The guard check is done by a person (operational).

cards.question: What does DLP stand for, and what does it do?
cards.answer: Data loss prevention. It stops sensitive data from leaving the company.
cards.explanation: It is a technical control: a system that protects.

cards.question: Give one example of each type of control: technical, operational and management.
cards.answer: Technical: a firewall. Operational: a security guard. Management: a policy.
cards.explanation: Ask yourself: is it a machine, a person or a rule?

cards.question: What is the difference between an IDS and an IPS?
cards.answer: An IDS spots an intrusion and warns you. An IPS spots it and blocks it.
cards.explanation: Both are technical controls.
cards.explanation_more: IDS means intrusion detection system and IPS means intrusion prevention system. This is outside the manual: the book only gives the letters.

cards.question: Which four verbs describe what a security control does?
cards.answer: It prevents, detects, minimizes or counteracts a threat.
cards.explanation: We stop, we spot, we reduce, we fight back.

paragraphes: A sports club plans a big tournament. Everyone shares ideas: the referees, the treasurer and the parents. But nobody has a common list.
So they forget first aid. They also buy the same balls twice.
A company that protects its data without a common plan makes the same mistake. The common plan has a name: a security control framework.

decouverte.titre: It is like a game manual
decouverte.comme: The manual of a board game says which pieces you need and how to play. Everybody follows the same manual.
decouverte.enVrai: A security control framework is the manual of security. It lists the company's processes (ways of doing things), procedures (steps) and solutions (tools). The framework does not play for you. You must apply it.

decouverte.question: Why does a company adopt a security control framework?
options: To stop needing its IT team
To follow the laws and protect its data better
To be sure it is never attacked
decouverte.answer: To follow the laws and protect its data better
decouverte.explanation: A framework helps a company follow laws and rules. This is called compliance. It also helps to build strong security. No framework can promise zero attacks.

decouverte.comme: A school and a swimming club do not have the same rules. The club has rules about caps and pools.
decouverte.enVrai: Companies often choose a framework for their industry. Card payments have the PCI framework. American hospitals have the HIPAA framework.

decouverte.texte: An online shop that keeps card numbers follows PCI. An American hospital keeps health data about its patients. This data is called PHI, or protected health information. The hospital follows HIPAA. Any company can also choose a general framework. These come from ISO/IEC, NIST or CIS. CIS is the Center for Internet Security.

HITRUST was made for healthcare companies. They have many different rules to follow. COBIT is a framework for all of a company's IT, not only security. To govern means to decide who decides and how things are checked.

cards.question: Official definition: “security control framework”
cards.answer: (ISC)2 defines a security control framework as "a notional construct outlining the organization's approach to security, including a list of specific security processes, procedures, and solutions used by the organization."
cards.explanation: A framework is a plan made of ideas. It describes how a company handles security. It lists the ways of working, the steps and the tools.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “security control framework”?
options: (ISC)2 defines a security control framework as "a notional construct outlining the organization's approach to security, including a list of specific security processes, procedures, and laws used by the organization."

(ISC)2 defines a security control framework as "a legal contract outlining the organization's approach to security, including a list of specific security processes, procedures, and solutions used by the organization."

(ISC)2 defines a security control framework as "a notional construct outlining the government's approach to security, including a list of specific security processes, procedures, and solutions used by the organization."

(ISC)2 defines a security control framework as "a notional construct outlining the organization's approach to security, including a list of specific security processes, procedures, and solutions used by the organization."
options_why: The list ends with solutions, not laws. A framework is not a law.
The word is notional: a construct of ideas. It is not a legal contract.
The framework outlines the approach of the organization, not of the government.
cards.answer: (ISC)2 defines a security control framework as "a notional construct outlining the organization's approach to security, including a list of specific security processes, procedures, and solutions used by the organization."
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: notional construct, approach to security, processes, procedures, and solutions.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “security control framework” from memory.
cards.answer: (ISC)2 defines a security control framework as "a notional construct outlining the organization's approach to security, including a list of specific security processes, procedures, and solutions used by the organization."
cards.explanation: Three parts: the approach of the organization, the list of processes and procedures, and the solutions it uses.

cards.question: Official definition: “PCI framework”
cards.answer: For example, the Payment Card Industry (PCI) control framework is a global framework used by financial services organizations and companies that handle cardholder data.
cards.explanation: PCI is a framework for companies that handle payment card data. Think of an online shop.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “PCI framework” from memory.
cards.answer: For example, the Payment Card Industry (PCI) control framework is a global framework used by financial services organizations and companies that handle cardholder data.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the name (payment cards), its global reach, and the card data it targets.

cards.question: Official definition: “HIPAA framework”
cards.answer: In the United States, the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) offers a control framework for healthcare organizations and companies that handle protected health information (PHI).
cards.explanation: HIPAA is an American framework for health care companies that handle patient health data.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “HIPAA framework” from memory.
cards.answer: In the United States, the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) offers a control framework for healthcare organizations and companies that handle protected health information (PHI).
cards.explanation: Three parts: the country, the control framework, and the health care sector.

cards.question: Official definition: “HITRUST”
cards.answer: The HITRUST (originally known as the Health Information Trust Alliance) Common Security Framework (CSF) was originally developed to address the overlapping regulatory environment in which many healthcare providers operate.
cards.explanation: HITRUST was made for healthcare companies. They had many rules that overlap, and it helps to handle them.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “HITRUST” from memory.
cards.answer: The HITRUST (originally known as the Health Information Trust Alliance) Common Security Framework (CSF) was originally developed to address the overlapping regulatory environment in which many healthcare providers operate.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the common framework, the problem (rules that overlap), and the healthcare providers.

cards.question: Official definition: “COBIT”
cards.answer: Control Objectives for Information Technologies (COBIT) is a framework developed by ISACA (previously known as the Information Systems Audit and Control Association) for overall information technology management and governance and is perhaps the most popular IT governance framework used in industry.
cards.explanation: COBIT organizes the management of all IT, not only security. It is very popular.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “COBIT” from memory.
cards.answer: Control Objectives for Information Technologies (COBIT) is a framework developed by ISACA (previously known as the Information Systems Audit and Control Association) for overall information technology management and governance and is perhaps the most popular IT governance framework used in industry.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the name, who made it (ISACA), and its fame in IT governance.

cards.question: Is a security control framework first a tool or a plan?
options: A tool that blocks attacks
A plan that organizes the protections
A law that every company must follow
A report about past attacks
options_why: A tool is only one solution inside the plan. A firewall is an example.
A framework is a set of ideas. A company chooses it.
A framework looks forward. It is not a report about the past.
cards.answer: A plan that organizes the protections
cards.explanation: The framework lists processes, procedures and solutions. It is a plan, not a single tool.

cards.question: An online shop keeps the bank card numbers of its customers. Which framework fits its industry?
options: HIPAA
PCI
COBIT
HITRUST
options_why: HIPAA targets American health care and patient data.
COBIT covers IT governance in general, not one industry.
HITRUST was first made for healthcare providers.
cards.answer: PCI
cards.explanation: PCI targets financial services and companies that handle cardholder data.

cards.question: An American hospital keeps patient health data. Which framework does the manual name for its industry?
options: HIPAA
PCI
COBIT
CIS Critical Security Controls
options_why: PCI targets payment card data, not patient records.
COBIT is a framework for IT governance. It is not tied to one industry.
The CIS Controls are general. They are not named for the health sector.
cards.answer: HIPAA
cards.explanation: HIPAA offers a control framework for health care in the United States.

cards.question: A company wants to follow the law and build a strong security program. What is the BEST reason to adopt a framework?
options: It guarantees that no attack will ever succeed against the company
It replaces the IT department of the company and its staff
It removes the need for written policies and procedures
It gives one common plan to meet legal rules and protect data
options_why: No framework can promise this. The answer is extreme.
People still run security. The framework only guides them.
Policies are still needed. The framework helps to write them.
cards.answer: It gives one common plan to meet legal rules and protect data
cards.explanation: A framework helps with legal and regulatory compliance and with confidentiality, integrity and availability.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT one of the five frameworks the manual says to know at a minimum?
options: ISO/IEC 27001
NIST Cybersecurity Framework
HIPAA
CIS Critical Security Controls
options_why: This is one of the five frameworks to know.
This is one of the five frameworks to know.
This is one of the five frameworks to know.
cards.answer: HIPAA
cards.explanation: The five are ISO 27001, ISO 27002, NIST 800-53, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the CIS Controls. HIPAA is an example for one sector.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Which of these is one of the five frameworks to know at a minimum?
options: PCI
COBIT
HITRUST
NIST 800-53
options_why: PCI is given as an example for one industry. It is not in the five.
COBIT is mentioned in a note. It is not in the five.
HITRUST is mentioned in a note. It is not in the five.
cards.answer: NIST 800-53
cards.explanation: NIST 800-53 is in the list of five. PCI, HITRUST and COBIT are mentioned separately.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: A new security manager joins a company with no framework. What should she do FIRST to start a top-down program?
options: Buy the most expensive security tools
Ask every worker to write their own rules
Choose a framework that fits the industry and the laws
Wait for a first attack to show what is missing
options_why: Tools come after the plan. They do not give the company a direction.
Many separate rules lead to the same problem as the tournament with no plan.
This is reactive. A manager prepares before the attack.
cards.answer: Choose a framework that fits the industry and the laws
cards.explanation: Strong governance starts with alignment with one or more security control frameworks.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Which framework is MOST focused on governing all IT, and not only security?
options: HIPAA
COBIT
PCI
HITRUST
options_why: HIPAA is a framework for health care in the United States.
PCI is for companies that handle payment card data.
HITRUST was made for healthcare providers with many rules.
cards.answer: COBIT
cards.explanation: COBIT describes end-to-end IT governance. Many security ideas are inside it, but it is not only about security.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks” (note).

cards.question: Many hospitals must obey rules that overlap. Which framework was MOST clearly made for this problem?
options: HITRUST
PCI
COBIT
NIST 800-53
options_why: PCI is about payment card data, not overlapping health rules.
COBIT is an IT governance framework for all industries.
It was first made to help American government agencies.
cards.answer: HITRUST
cards.explanation: HITRUST was first developed for the overlapping rules that healthcare providers face.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks” (note).

cards.question: What does PHI stand for?
cards.answer: Protected health information, such as the medical records of patients.
cards.explanation: HIPAA is the framework built around PHI.

cards.question: Which two ISO/IEC standards must you know at a minimum?
cards.answer: ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27002.
cards.explanation: You will study them in the next planets.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Which two NIST publications must you know at a minimum, and what is the fifth framework?
cards.answer: NIST 800-53 and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework. The fifth is the CIS Critical Security Controls.
cards.explanation: Five frameworks in all: two from ISO/IEC, two from NIST, one from CIS.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: What does strong governance start with, for an effective top-down approach?
cards.answer: Aligning with one or more security control frameworks.
cards.explanation: The leaders choose a framework, then the plans and rules follow it.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks”.

cards.question: Is COBIT a framework made only for security?
cards.answer: No. COBIT describes the governance of all IT, with many security ideas inside.
cards.explanation: COBIT is broad. Security is only one part of it.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Security Control Frameworks” (note).

paragraphes: A school canteen serves hundreds of meals a day. To keep everyone healthy, it needs hygiene rules, trained cooks and regular checks.
Each cook does not invent these rules. They come from a standard. A standard is a common rule written by experts and used everywhere.
In information security, the best-known standard is ISO/IEC 27001.

decouverte.titre: It is like the hygiene system of the canteen
decouverte.comme: The canteen has people (the cooks), ways of working (washing hands) and tools (fridges). Together they keep the food safe.
decouverte.enVrai: An ISMS does the same for information. ISMS means information security management system. It is a set of people, processes and technologies. ISO 27001 describes the parts of an ISMS. It does not give you the tools.

decouverte.question: ISO 27001 is a standard. What does it mostly describe?
options: Which firewalls to buy for your network
How to organize a security management system
Which laws apply in each country
decouverte.answer: How to organize a security management system
decouverte.explanation: It describes the parts of an ISMS. It does not choose brands of tools. It is not a law.

decouverte.texte: The manual says ISO 27001 was last revised in 2013. It has 114 controls in 14 domains. A domain is a big theme, like access control or encryption. Its parent, ISO/IEC 27000, was revised in 2018.

decouverte.comme: Your report card has several subjects, like math, sports and languages. Each subject has its own grades.
decouverte.enVrai: ISO 27001 sorts its 114 controls into 14 domains. A domain is a big theme of security, like a school subject.

cards.question: Official definition: “ISO/IEC 27001”
cards.answer: ISO/IEC 27001 (sometimes referred to as just ISO 27001) is an information security standard published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC).
cards.explanation: ISO 27001 is a security standard. Two groups publish it: ISO and IEC.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “ISO/IEC 27001”?
options: ISO/IEC 27001 (sometimes referred to as just ISO 27001) is an information security law published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC).

ISO/IEC 27001 (sometimes referred to as just ISO 27001) is an information security standard published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).

ISO/IEC 27001 (sometimes referred to as just ISO 27001) is a network design standard published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC).

ISO/IEC 27001 (sometimes referred to as just ISO 27001) is an information security standard published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC).
options_why: A standard is not a law. A company chooses to follow it.
The two publishers are ISO and IEC. NIST is a different group.
It is about information security, not about network design.
cards.answer: ISO/IEC 27001 (sometimes referred to as just ISO 27001) is an information security standard published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC).
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: information security standard, ISO, and IEC.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “ISO/IEC 27001” from memory.
cards.answer: ISO/IEC 27001 (sometimes referred to as just ISO 27001) is an information security standard published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC).
cards.explanation: Three parts: the type (an information security standard) and the two publishers, ISO and IEC.

cards.question: Official definition: “ISO 27001 and ISMS”
cards.answer: ISO 27001 is the most popular standard within the ISO/IEC 27000 family of standards and is focused on the creation and maintenance of an information security management system (ISMS), which ISO defines as "a systematic approach to managing sensitive company information so that it remains secure."
cards.explanation: ISO 27001 is the best-known standard of its family. It helps a company build and keep an ISMS. An ISMS is an organized way to keep company information safe.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “ISO 27001 and ISMS”?
options: ISO 27001 is the newest standard within the ISO/IEC 27000 family of standards and is focused on the creation and maintenance of an information security management system (ISMS), which ISO defines as "a systematic approach to managing sensitive company information so that it remains secure."

ISO 27001 is the most popular standard within the ISO/IEC 27000 family of standards and is focused on the creation and maintenance of an information security management system (ISMS), which ISO defines as "a systematic approach to managing sensitive company information so that it remains secure."

ISO 27001 is the most popular standard within the ISO/IEC 27000 family of standards and is focused on the creation and maintenance of an information security management system (ISMS), which ISO defines as "a flexible approach to managing sensitive company information so that it remains secure."

ISO 27001 is the most popular standard within the ISO/IEC 27000 family of standards and is focused on the creation and testing of an information security management system (ISMS), which ISO defines as "a systematic approach to managing sensitive company information so that it remains secure."
options_why: The manual says most popular, not newest.
The word is systematic: organized and planned. It is not flexible.
The focus is creation and maintenance, not creation and testing.
cards.answer: ISO 27001 is the most popular standard within the ISO/IEC 27000 family of standards and is focused on the creation and maintenance of an information security management system (ISMS), which ISO defines as "a systematic approach to managing sensitive company information so that it remains secure."
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: most popular, creation and maintenance, systematic approach.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “ISO 27001 and ISMS” from memory.
cards.answer: ISO 27001 is the most popular standard within the ISO/IEC 27000 family of standards and is focused on the creation and maintenance of an information security management system (ISMS), which ISO defines as "a systematic approach to managing sensitive company information so that it remains secure."
cards.explanation: Three parts: the most popular standard, the creation and maintenance of an ISMS, and the ISO definition: a systematic approach.

cards.question: Official definition: “ISMS, in simple terms”
cards.answer: In plain English, an ISMS is a set of people, processes, and technologies that manages the overall security of a company's systems and data.
cards.explanation: An ISMS is people, ways of working and tools. Together they keep the systems and data of a company safe.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “ISMS, in simple terms” from memory.
cards.answer: In plain English, an ISMS is a set of people, processes, and technologies that manages the overall security of a company's systems and data.
cards.explanation: Three parts: people, processes and technologies, the overall security, and what it protects: systems and data.

cards.question: Is an ISMS mostly a software product, or a set of people, processes and technologies?
options: A set of people, processes and technologies
One software product that protects all computers
A group of laws that apply to the company
A report that an auditor writes every year
options_why: Software is only one part. An ISMS also needs people and ways of working.
An ISMS is not a law. It is how the company organizes its own security.
A report only describes. An ISMS is a system that manages security.
cards.answer: A set of people, processes and technologies
cards.explanation: An ISMS mixes people, ways of working and tools. A piece of software is only one part.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: A company wants to build an ISMS with the most popular standard of the ISO/IEC 27000 family. Which one does it choose?
options: ISO/IEC 27002
NIST 800-53
ISO/IEC 27001
PCI
options_why: It builds on 27001 and gives advice on controls. It is covered in the next planet.
This is an American catalog of controls, not part of the ISO family.
PCI targets payment card data. It is not part of the ISO family.
cards.answer: ISO/IEC 27001
cards.explanation: The manual calls ISO 27001 the most popular standard of its family. It is focused on creating and keeping an ISMS.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: How many controls and domains does ISO 27001:2013 have?
options: 114 controls in 14 domains
14 controls in 114 domains
108 controls in 23 domains
20 controls in 18 domains
options_why: The numbers are swapped. There are more controls than domains.
These numbers belong to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, not to ISO 27001.
These numbers mix up the CIS Controls and the NIST 800-53 families.
cards.answer: 114 controls in 14 domains
cards.explanation: ISO 27001:2013 has 114 controls across 14 domains.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: A company has rules, trained staff and security tools. But nobody manages them together. What would an ISMS BEST give this company?
options: A new firewall that replaces the old tools
A new law that forces all the staff to follow the company rules
One system that manages people, processes and technologies
A promise that no attack will ever succeed
options_why: A new tool does not join the rules, the staff and the tools into one whole.
An ISMS is not a law. It is a management system.
No system can promise this. The answer is extreme.
cards.answer: One system that manages people, processes and technologies
cards.explanation: An ISMS is a set of people, processes and technologies that manages the overall security of the company.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: Which statement about ISO 27001 is MOST accurate?
options: It tells each company exactly which brand of tool it must buy for its network
It is a law that every company must follow
It only covers computer networks and nothing else
It describes the parts of an ISMS and is the basis of many programs
options_why: A standard says what to organize, not which brand to buy.
ISO standards are not laws. A company chooses to follow them.
It covers the overall security of systems and data, with 14 domains.
cards.answer: It describes the parts of an ISMS and is the basis of many programs
cards.explanation: The manual says ISO 27001 describes the overall components of an ISMS and is the basis for many security programs.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: Which of these is one of the 14 domains of ISO 27001?
options: Network design
Supplier relationships
Employee payroll
Software licensing
options_why: This is not one of the 14 domains.
This is not one of the 14 domains.
This is not one of the 14 domains.
cards.answer: Supplier relationships
cards.explanation: Supplier relationships is one of the 14 domains. It covers the outside companies that work with you.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT one of the 14 domains of ISO 27001?
options: Cryptography
Compliance
Asset management
Customer support
options_why: This is one of the 14 domains.
This is one of the 14 domains.
This is one of the 14 domains.
cards.answer: Customer support
cards.explanation: Customer support is not in the list. The 14 domains are security themes.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: A company wants to decide who can open which folder. Which ISO 27001 domain covers this BEST?
options: Access control
Asset management
Cryptography
Compliance
options_why: This domain makes the list of what the company must protect.
This domain is about hiding data with secret codes.
This domain checks that the company follows the laws and its own rules.
cards.answer: Access control
cards.explanation: Deciding who may open what is access control.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: A company checks the past of a job candidate before hiring. Which ISO 27001 domain is BEST for this?
options: Access control
Human resource security
Asset management
Organization of information security
options_why: This domain decides who may open what, after the person is hired.
This domain is about the things the company must protect.
This domain is about who is responsible for which part of security.
cards.answer: Human resource security
cards.explanation: Checking and training the people of the company is human resource security.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: A company installs smoke detectors and protects its server room against floods. Which domain is the BEST match?
options: System acquisition, development, and maintenance
Information security incident management
Physical and environmental security
Communications security
options_why: This domain is about the security of software and systems that the company buys or builds.
This domain is about reacting to an attack as it happens.
This domain is about protecting the data that travels across the network.
cards.answer: Physical and environmental security
cards.explanation: Fire and water are dangers to the building and its equipment. This is physical and environmental security.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: A company checks that it follows the laws and its own rules. Which domain covers this?
options: Operations security
Supplier relationships
Organization of information security
Compliance
options_why: This domain is about the daily running of systems.
This domain is about the outside companies that work with you.
This domain is about who is responsible for which part of security.
cards.answer: Compliance
cards.explanation: Following the laws and the company rules is compliance.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: What do the letters ISMS stand for?
cards.answer: Information security management system.
cards.explanation: It is a set of people, processes and technologies.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: In which year was ISO 27001 last revised, according to the manual?
cards.answer: In 2013. Its parent standard, ISO/IEC 27000, was revised in 2018.
cards.explanation: Two years not to mix up: 2013 for the 27001, 2018 for the 27000.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: Which ISO 27001 domain is about deciding who is responsible for each part of security?
cards.answer: Organization of information security.
cards.explanation: Think of naming a security manager and defining the role.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: Which ISO 27001 domain is about making a list of the things the company must protect?
cards.answer: Asset management.
cards.explanation: An asset is something of value, like a computer or a file.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

cards.question: Which ISO 27001 domain is about hiding data with secret codes?
cards.answer: Cryptography.
cards.explanation: Think of encrypting a hard drive.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27001”.

paragraphes: Your school decides to have a rulebook. Good idea. But each teacher asks: what should I do in my classroom?
The school needs a second, more exact document. It gives advice step by step.
In information security, ISO 27001 says what to organize: an ISMS. ISMS means information security management system. The second document is ISO/IEC 27002.

decouverte.titre: The meal plan and the recipe
decouverte.comme: A meal plan says: a starter, a main dish and a dessert. A recipe says how much flour you need and how long to cook.
decouverte.enVrai: ISO 27001 gives the plan: the parts of an ISMS. ISO 27002 gives the recipe: best practices to choose, set up and manage controls. People say it is more prescriptive. This means it says more exactly what to do.

decouverte.question: Which standard tells you more exactly which controls to choose and how to manage them?
options: ISO/IEC 27001
ISO/IEC 27002
decouverte.explanation: ISO 27001 describes the system, the ISMS. ISO 27002 gives best-practice advice for the controls. The two go together.

decouverte.texte: The title of ISO/IEC 27002 is Security Techniques, Code of practice for information security controls. A code of practice is a set of best practices. The word controls means the protections of the company.
A small school and a big bank face different dangers. ISO 27002 helps each one choose its controls by its risk profile. The risk profile is the kind and the size of its dangers.

cards.question: Official definition: “ISO/IEC 27002”
cards.answer: ISO/IEC 27002 (again, often referred to as just ISO 27002) is titled "Security Techniques — Code of practice for information security controls."
cards.explanation: This is the title of the standard. It is a set of best practices for security controls.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27002”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “ISO/IEC 27002”?
options: ISO/IEC 27002 (again, often referred to as just ISO 27002) is titled "Security Techniques — Code of practice for information security controls."
ISO/IEC 27002 (again, often referred to as just ISO 27002) is titled "Security Policies — Code of practice for information security controls."
ISO/IEC 27002 (again, often referred to as just ISO 27002) is titled "Security Techniques — Code of conduct for information security controls."
ISO/IEC 27002 (again, often referred to as just ISO 27002) is titled "Security Techniques — Code of practice for information security audits."
options_why: The title begins with Security Techniques, not Security Policies.
It is a Code of practice, not a code of conduct.
The title ends with controls, not audits.
cards.answer: ISO/IEC 27002 (again, often referred to as just ISO 27002) is titled "Security Techniques — Code of practice for information security controls."
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: Security Techniques, Code of practice, information security controls.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “ISO/IEC 27002” from memory.
cards.answer: ISO/IEC 27002 (again, often referred to as just ISO 27002) is titled "Security Techniques — Code of practice for information security controls."
cards.explanation: Three parts of the title: Security Techniques, Code of practice, and information security controls.

cards.question: Official definition: “ISO/IEC 27002, what the standard provides”
cards.answer: This standard builds on ISO 27001 by providing guidelines for organizations to select, implement, and manage security controls based on their own security risk profile.
cards.explanation: It adds advice to ISO 27001. It helps a company choose, set up and manage the controls that fit its own risks.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27002”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “ISO/IEC 27002, what the standard provides”?
options: This standard replaces ISO 27001 by providing guidelines for organizations to select, implement, and manage security controls based on their own security risk profile.
This standard builds on ISO 27001 by providing guidelines for organizations to select, implement, and manage security controls based on their own security risk profile.
This standard builds on ISO 27001 by providing laws for organizations to select, implement, and manage security controls based on their own security risk profile.
This standard builds on ISO 27001 by providing guidelines for organizations to select, implement, and manage security controls based on the average risk profile of their industry.
options_why: It builds on ISO 27001. It does not replace it.
It gives guidelines, which are advice. It does not give laws.
The profile is the own risk profile of each organization, not an average.
cards.answer: This standard builds on ISO 27001 by providing guidelines for organizations to select, implement, and manage security controls based on their own security risk profile.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: builds on ISO 27001, guidelines, select, implement, and manage, own risk profile.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “ISO/IEC 27002, what the standard provides” from memory.
cards.answer: This standard builds on ISO 27001 by providing guidelines for organizations to select, implement, and manage security controls based on their own security risk profile.
cards.explanation: Three parts: it builds on ISO 27001, the three verbs select, implement and manage, and the own risk profile.

cards.question: Official definition: “ISO 27002, more prescriptive”
cards.answer: In other words, ISO 27002 is a bit more prescriptive than ISO 27001, as it provides best-practice recommendations for organizations to build and maintain their ISMSs.
cards.explanation: ISO 27002 says more exactly what to do. It gives best-practice advice to build and keep an ISMS.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27002”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “ISO 27002, more prescriptive” from memory.
cards.answer: In other words, ISO 27002 is a bit more prescriptive than ISO 27001, as it provides best-practice recommendations for organizations to build and maintain their ISMSs.
cards.explanation: Three parts: a bit more prescriptive, best-practice recommendations, and build and maintain the ISMS.

cards.question: Which of the two standards is more prescriptive?
options: ISO/IEC 27001
They are equally prescriptive
ISO/IEC 27002
Neither, because both are laws
options_why: ISO 27001 describes the overall parts of an ISMS. It is more general.
The manual says ISO 27002 is a bit more prescriptive than ISO 27001.
Neither is a law. Both are standards that a company chooses.
cards.answer: ISO/IEC 27002
cards.explanation: ISO 27002 gives best-practice recommendations, so it says more exactly what to do.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “ISO/IEC 27002”.

cards.question: A company already has an ISMS. It wants advice on how to choose and manage its controls. Which standard should it read?
options: ISO/IEC 27002
ISO/IEC 27001
HIPAA

decouverte.titre: The fire plan of the school
paragraphes: A school wants to be ready for fires. It lists its rooms, installs detectors and holds drills. It also knows how to repair the damage after a fire.
These actions never stop. They happen all year, at the same time.
The NIST Cybersecurity Framework, or CSF, organizes computer security in this way.

decouverte.comme: Facing a fire, we know what we must protect, we install protections, we detect smoke, we react, and we repair.

decouverte.texte: The NIST CSF was first published in 2014. Version 1.1 came out in 2018. The five functions are split into 23 categories. These are split into 108 subcategories. A subcategory describes one specific control or one desired result.

decouverte.comme: A rulebook of 300 pages is hard to adapt. A one-page pocket guide is easier to adapt to your club.
decouverte.enVrai: The NIST CSF lines up with NIST 800-53 and other frameworks. But it was designed to be more flexible and easier to understand. Private companies can adapt it more easily.

decouverte.enVrai: Identify: understand what you must protect. Protect: put protections in place. Detect: notice that something is happening. Respond: act when an incident is found.
